text:
jordy: Quick sanity check — did a terraform change to add the new telemetry SA annotation and now some staging pods are failing to mount secrets. Seems like we ended up with both an IRSA annotation *and* an explicit secret mount for creds on the same deployment. Anyone seen this pattern before?

jordy: snippet from the service account we applied (k8s resource managed by TF):
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: telemetry-uploader
  namespace: team-foo
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-telemetry
automountServiceAccountToken: true
```

jordy: and the helm chart values we also set (older pattern):
```yaml
extraSecretMounts:
  - name: telemetry-creds
    path: /etc/telemetry/creds.json
    secretName: telemetry-creds-team-foo
```

jordy: result: new pods around the rollout time show both the projected token (IRSA) and still trying to read the old secret file which is gone after a TF rename — crashloop on init container. Not sure best minimal-downtime fix. options I see: 1) re-add secret temporarily, 2) remove extraSecretMounts from helm and rollout, 3) patch pods to stop expecting file (not possible).

jordy: also curious — if I add the eks annotation to the SA via kubectl or TF, do existing pods pick up the projected token automatically or do they need to be restarted? :thinking:

michelle: yep this is a common Helm vs TF overlap. Short answers: annotate SA -> existing pods do NOT magically get a new projected token path they were not configured to mount. Pod spec contains projected token volume at creation. So you need a pod restart to pick up IRSA.

michelle: quick steps I usually do: 1) patch the helm values (remove extraSecretMounts) in a new chart revision, 2) do a canary rollout (scale down old RC / rollout restart) for a subset to validate, 3) once canary is green, roll the rest. If you need zero-downtime and can't afford restart, re-create the secret with the old name pointing to a no-op JSON for the init container, then remove after safe rollouts.

michelle: commands to inspect which pods have the secret mount vs projected token:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n team-foo -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{"\n"}{range .spec.volumes[*]}{.name}:{.projected?"projected":""}{" "}{end}{"---\n"}{end}'
# or for mounts in containers:
kubectl get pods -n team-foo -o json | jq -r '.items[] | {name:.metadata.name, mounts:.spec.containers[].volumeMounts}'
```

sam: Agreed with michelle. Additional TF notes: if the SA is managed by TF, prefer adding the eks annotation in the kubernetes_service_account resource so we don’t have drift. If Helm is injecting a secretMount via values, remove that from values and let Helm reconcile. If TF already renamed the secret, re-create the secret name as a short-lived shim to get through the rollout.

sam: Also watch for lifecycle "ignore_changes" on automountServiceAccountToken — we've done that before and it bit us (state drift). Better to let k8s reflect the desired automount flag in TF/Helm consistently.

alex: +1 on restart requirement. Projected token is mounted as a volume at pod creation; adding the SA annotation doesn't change existing pod specs. So either restart pods or mount shim secret.

alex: If you do go the secret shim route, ensure the secret has the same keys the init container expects (or make it an empty file) so init container exits cleanly, otherwise you'll still crash.

deploy-bot: Heads up — there is a terraform apply queued for infra/staging in ~10m (plan ID tfplan-2026-03-17-12). If you want to gate that, comment on PR: https://terraform.example.corp/pulls/42

jordy: awesome, thanks. Plan: I will patch the Helm values to remove extraSecretMounts in a canary chart and hold the TF apply. I'll also recreate the old secret name with a minimal creds.json for 1 hour so init containers don't fail during canary. Will post the canary pod names here when started. :shipit:

michelle: sounds good — ping me when canary up, I'll watch logs and access requests.

jordy: will do. thanks all!
